existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `Substance` has high-impact local breaking changes: `code` has a new `CodeableReference` representation, `instance` was removed/flattened, and `ingredient` was removed. The main uncertainty is the intended official migration path for package/container and ingredient data.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is not just a field rename. Systems must adopt the R6 `CodeableReference` wire shape, decide how to create or reference `SubstanceDefinition`, flatten at most one set of package/container details into top-level `expiry` and `quantity`, and move composition data out of `Substance`. Lossless migration is doubtful for repeated R4 `instance` entries or ingredient records without additional business rules.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the computable StructureDefinition deltas because the R4 and R6 local differentials and snapshots agree. Confidence is lower for intended semantic mappings because official narrative diffs, ConceptMaps, and terminology expansions were not supplied.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
Substance keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 3 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 0 potential hard break(s), 2 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 1 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 2, which creates neutral stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 36/100, producing migration shape `moderate-targeted-remodel`, major migration `Partial`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Use less-breaking designs where they do not preserve obsolete or conflicting models indefinitely.

topFindings.title: Repeatable Substance.instance backbone was removed and only partly flattened
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and R6-to-R4 loss: any R4 payload using `Substance.instance` is invalid as R6, and multiple package/container groups cannot be faithfully represented by the single top-level R6 fields without splitting resources or adding non-base data.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Substance.ingredient backbone was removed from the resource
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: R4 inline ingredient content is not accepted on R6 Substance, and business logic or SDK properties for inline composition disappear. Reverse loss is limited for this path because R6 Substance has no replacement inline ingredient field.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Substance.code changed from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference(SubstanceDefinition)
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: R4 concept-shaped JSON at `Substance.code` is not the R6 CodeableReference child shape, and generated models/search expressions change; R6 reference-only values also create R6-to-R4 loss unless resolved.

topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation and R6-to-R4 loss: validation does not fail, but the same field now mixes material identifiers and package/container identifiers, making old assumptions and reverse mapping ambiguous.
